title: Fraction Calculator: how it works, formula and examples
excerpt: Fraction Calculator: Add, subtract, multiply and divide fractions. Learn how to use it, the formula behind it, a worked example and answers to common questions.
content:
The [Fraction Calculator](/fraction-calculator) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Add, subtract, multiply and divide fractions. Enter your numerator 1, denominator 1, operation, numerator 2 and denominator 2 and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

A fraction calculator performs arithmetic on fractions and reduces the answer to its simplest form, with mixed-number and decimal equivalents. This guide explains how to use it, the formula it applies, and a worked example you can follow with your own numbers. Related Math tools include [Percentage Calculator](/percentage-calculator), [Square Root Calculator](/square-root-calculator) and [Average Calculator](/average-calculator). People also look for this tool as "adding fractions calculator", "simplify fractions", "fraction to decimal".

## How to use the Fraction Calculator

Start by entering your numerator 1, then entering your denominator 1, choosing your operation from the list, entering your numerator 2 and finally entering your denominator 2. The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause. When you want a clean slate, Reset restores the defaults.

1. Enter your numerator 1.
2. Enter your denominator 1.
3. Choose your operation from the list.
4. Enter your numerator 2.
5. Enter your denominator 2.
6. Check the result — it updates instantly as you type.

## Formula

a/b + c/d = (ad + bc)/bd. a/b × c/d = ac/bd. a/b ÷ c/d = ad/bc. Simplify by dividing by the greatest common divisor.

That is the standard formula for this calculation, and it is the same one the [Fraction Calculator](/fraction-calculator) applies to the values you enter. You can work it out by hand, but the calculator is faster when you want to try several values, and it removes the risk of a slip in the arithmetic. If the figures look wrong, check your inputs first — a misplaced decimal point is the usual culprit.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. 3/4 + 2/5 = 15/20 + 8/20 = 23/20 = 1 3/20 = 1.15. Try the same figures in the [Fraction Calculator](/fraction-calculator) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves. The steps are the same whatever numbers you use; only the figures change.

## What the result shows

With the default values (Numerator 1: 3, Denominator 1: 4, Operation: +, Numerator 2: 2, Denominator 2: 5), the [Fraction Calculator](/fraction-calculator) returns Result (simplified): 23/20, Mixed number: 1 3/20, Decimal: 1.15. The first figure is the headline result, and the rest break it down so you can see how the total is made up. Change any value and every figure updates instantly. If you want to compare with a related calculation, the [Percentage Calculator](/percentage-calculator) is worth a look before you finish.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- To divide, multiply by the reciprocal.
- Simplify before multiplying to keep numbers small.

Keep these in mind and the figures will be as useful as the numbers you put in.

## Frequently asked questions

### How do I simplify a fraction?

Divide the numerator and denominator by their greatest common divisor. Try it with your own numbers in the [Fraction Calculator](/fraction-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### How do I convert a fraction to a decimal?

Divide the numerator by the denominator. Try it with your own numbers in the [Fraction Calculator](/fraction-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What formula does the Fraction Calculator use?

a/b + c/d = (ad + bc)/bd. a/b × c/d = ac/bd. a/b ÷ c/d = ad/bc. Simplify by dividing by the greatest common divisor. You can see it in action in the [Fraction Calculator](/fraction-calculator) — enter your own values and the result updates as you type.

### What do I need to use the Fraction Calculator?

Just Numerator 1, Denominator 1, Operation, Numerator 2 and Denominator 2. Enter those values and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. If you are unsure about a value, try a rough figure first and then refine it — the result updates instantly.
